name: Cate Le Bon
label: Mexican Summer
lede: A Welsh farm kid who sang on a Gruff Rhys tour, built her own chair, and ended up the person Wilco, Deerhunter and St. Vincent call when they want to sound less like themselves.

eras.title: A farm in Penboyr, a Casio, a patron
eras.text: Born Cate Timothy in Carmarthenshire, she borrowed her stage name from Simon Le Bon and got her first break singing behind other people. By the end of the decade she had a debut album and a mentor in Super Furry Animals' Gruff Rhys.

years.h: Backing vocals on Richard James's The Seven Sleepers Den
years.p: Her first recorded appearance is singing behind the Gorky's Zygotic Mynci singer [[Richard James|6966324a-c29f-4b6f-92a4-5e34ad2abab3]], still under her birth name, Cate Timothy.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · NPR Music · Irish Times
years.h: Supporting Gruff Rhys, who then takes her under his wing
years.p: She opens for [[Gruff Rhys|254caf14-7b63-47d1-aa9f-acc7cb541814]] of [[Super Furry Animals|c5f5dc27-3059-49c0-ae45-5009a01bb9ec]] on his solo UK tour. NPR reported he first spotted her at Welsh club nights and became her mentor.
years.xp:
Rhys described her first single, the double A-side 'No One Can Drag Me Down' and 'Disappear', as 'Bobbie Gentry and Nico fight over a Casio keyboard; melody wins!', per Wikipedia.

He also later lent her a house: the Victorian terrace in Cardiff where she wrote Pompeii belongs to Rhys, the Irish Times reported.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Edrych yn Llygad Ceffyl Benthyg: a Welsh-language EP on Peski
years.p: Her first release under her own name is sung in Welsh and comes out on Peski Records, with [[Gorky's Zygotic Mynci|4015f3f8-2711-41de-b80b-4fee07373b12]] players Megan Childs on violin and John Thomas on pedal steel.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · Irish Times
years.h: Singing 'I Lust U' on Neon Neon's Stainless Style
years.p: She is the guest voice on the single from [[Neon Neon|6191360a-edc5-41d7-a83e-c9f0ab842f53]], Gruff Rhys and Boom Bip's concept album about the DeLorean factory in Belfast.

years.src: Wikipedia: Me Oh My · NPR Music · Bandcamp Daily
years.h: Me Oh My: the debut, on Irony Bored
years.p: Released 12 October 2009. Slow, dry and deadpan enough that reviewers reached for Nico.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports the album was first going to be called Pet Deaths. A Welsh-language song, 'O am Gariad', was written for it and cut because it interrupted the flow.

NPR credited Rhys with producing it and called the result bare-bones.

eras.title: Eigg, then Los Angeles
eras.text: The second album gets busier and stranger, and in January 2013 she leaves Cardiff for California. The move sets up the band, the sound and the collaborators that run through the next decade.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cyrk · Bandcamp Daily
years.h: Cyrk, written with the Isle of Eigg in her head
years.p: Faster and more dissonant than Me Oh My. She called it a time-travel travelogue, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says she drew on the sea, wildlife and matters of the heart on Eigg in the Inner Hebrides, and rehearsed with a tight Welsh band in the mountains.

Bandcamp Daily points to the closing pair 'Ploughing Out, Pt. 1' and 'Pt. 2' as the turn: the second is fuzzy, Stereolab-ish rock with skronky saxophone.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · Wikipedia: Mug Museum
years.h: She moves from Wales to Los Angeles
years.p: Le Bon relocates to LA to push her career in the US, and Mug Museum gets recorded there that spring at Seahorse Sound.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mug Museum · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Mug Museum: her first record on Wichita and Turnstile
years.p: Released 12 November 2013, produced by [[Noah Georgeson|cacf76c5-f3f2-4c35-ba0c-d3f2a07c3949]] and [[Josiah Steinbrick|3143853f-44ce-49d5-b7ec-b59e8a6cf871]]. Pitchfork gave it 7.3.
years.xp:
Jeremy Larson wrote in Pitchfork that it has small, graceful songs with deceptive amounts of depth. [[Stephen Black|d3789f6f-cc8d-4404-a104-103f9daa6bd3]] played bass and [[H. Hawkline|ae41819a-51e2-4f21-aa3c-b37f22b733ae]] (Huw Evans) guitar.

The title came from a former roommate's name for the pile of teacups in her bedroom.

years.src: NPR Music
years.h: She hand-makes about 150 ceramic mugs for pre-orders
years.p: NPR reported she threw the mugs herself for the Mug Museum campaign, which is the kind of detail her fans repeat.

eras.title: DRINKS, Crab Day and a woodworking course
eras.text: Le Bon finds the people she will keep working with, including Tim Presley, and then abruptly steps away from touring to study furniture. The chair she builds becomes the picture of her next record.

years.cap: Cate le Bon performing at Glastonbury Festival in 2014 · Wikimedia
years.src: NPR Music · Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: DRINKS: [[Tim Presley|25f6404b-4738-48a2-b1e0-465b7430fb93]] and Le Bon make Hermits on Holiday
years.p: Presley's band opened for her in LA, per NPR. The duo record as DRINKS and release the album on Heavenly Recordings in August 2015.
years.xp:
Presley told NPR she completely rearranged one of his songs and made it ten million times better than what he had. Le Bon said the project reignited her love of writing and performing.

Bandcamp Daily called it lean and loose, two fringe-pop wizards in experimental mode. NPR premiered the title track in May 2015. Presley, of [[White Fence|68548de4-c045-426a-9745-b52a8a22d2d2]] and [[Darker My Love|15c5c0de-b8ff-49ab-8a58-506c89453f03]], would later be her partner for years.

years.src: Wikipedia: Crab Day · NPR Music
years.h: Crab Day: her first on Drag City, written at Stinson Beach
years.p: Released 15 April 2016, recorded at Panoramic House in Stinson Beach, California, with [[Stella Mozgawa|f578d602-2ed4-4ec4-a0a7-1947cb01ac44]] on drums and Stephen Black on bass. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp:
Laura Snapes wrote in Pitchfork that it is a voyage into doubt led by a queasy compass.

NPR reported she called it the first record she has made with no inhibition at all, and that it felt like a band's record rather than hers.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · NPR Music
years.h: BANANA: Le Bon's five-piece improvising band, in mohair hats
years.p: The Crab Day lineup tours as BANANA with Stephen Black, Huw Evans, [[Josh Klinghoffer|3f6e1477-03dc-4117-ac15-ec53b776e9a0]] and Josiah Steinbrick. A BANANA live album follows on Leaving Records in 2017.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Rock Pool EP on Drag City
years.p: Four tracks, including her version of 'I Just Want to Be Good', written for Sweet Baboo's 2015 album The Boombox Ballads.

years.big: 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., in the Lake District
q: disgruntled accountants, retired dentists, a real pick-and-mix of people
Cate Le Bon on her classmates (Rolling Stone)
years.src: Rolling Stone · Irish Times
years.h: She quits the road for a yearlong furniture course
years.p: Burnt out, Le Bon spends a year learning woodworking, and writes Reward on a secondhand piano between classes.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone reported the course ran to a strict schedule and was incredible and at times quite challenging, in her words. When it finished she built a chair in dark-stained oak.

She told the magazine the chair looked like the record sounded in her mind. It lives at her parents' house in West Wales.

eras.title: Marfa, Mexican Summer and Mercury
eras.text: Everything she has been building comes at once: a new label, a duo record, a desert session with Bradford Cox and the piano album that gets her nominated for the Mercury Prize. She also stops being only an artist and becomes somebody else's producer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hippo Lite
years.h: DRINKS make Hippo Lite, Pitchfork gives it 8.0
years.p: Released 20 April 2018 on Drag City. Reviews ran from 3/10 at Exclaim! to 9/10 at Loud and Quiet.
years.xp: Stephen Black engineered it, per Wikipedia, and John Thomas II played extra drums. A DIY reviewer praised moments of sheer chaotic genius married with brilliant songwriting.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: She signs with the Brooklyn label Mexican Summer
years.p: The move from Drag City to Mexican Summer sets her up for Reward, Pompeii and Michelangelo Dying.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · Wikipedia: Michelangelo Dying
years.h: Onstage with John Cale at the Barbican
years.p: She plays with [[John Cale|72c090b6-a68e-4cb9-b330-85278681a714]] and the London Contemporary Orchestra at the Barbican Centre, a link that comes back when Cale sings on her 2025 album.

years.src: Stereogum · Bandcamp Daily · Rolling Stone
years.h: At Marfa Myths, Bradford Cox invites her to produce Deerhunter
years.p: [[Bradford Cox|da7eb8d4-4a74-474f-b907-c38d2355b72b]] told Stereogum she would produce the next [[Deerhunter|4f416ed7-dda2-45de-a6f1-b986e861cf4b]] record in Marfa, Texas, informed by the desert around it. The pair also record a quick-and-loose EP, Myths 004.
years.xp:
Cox said there is a feeling of disappearance in Marfa, and that the desert has a lot of disappeared things in it. That became the title of the album.

Le Bon called Myths 004 a crude holiday scrapbook of studio jams, per Bandcamp Daily.

years.cap: Deerhunter, Why Hasn't Everything Already Disappeared?
years.src: Wikipedia: Why Hasn't Everything Already Disappeared?
years.h: She co-produces Deerhunter's Why Hasn't Everything Already Disappeared?
years.p: Released 18 January 2019 on 4AD, with sessions in Marfa, Texas, and Atlanta. Le Bon also plays harpsichord, mandolin and sings on it.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits her as co-producer with Ben H. Allen III, Ben Etter and the band. She plays harpsichord on 'Death in Midsummer', sings on 'Tarnung' and plays mandolin on 'No One's Sleeping'.

Pitchfork gave the album 8.0.

years.src: Wikipedia: Reward · Rolling Stone · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Reward: the piano record, and a Mercury Prize nomination
years.p: Released 24 May 2019 on Mexican Summer. Pitchfork gave it 8.4; it earned her a Mercury Prize nomination.
years.xp:
Produced by Le Bon, [[Samur Khouja|a6f84fad-37f1-4d77-8ab1-38c93cdc81fc]] and Josiah Steinbrick. Kurt Vile sings on one track; Klinghoffer, Mozgawa, Black and Hawkline play.

Sessions ran at Stinson Beach in May, in LA, and in Joshua Tree that August. Of the LA sessions she told Rolling Stone: 'Everything went to shit.'

eras.title: Stranded in Cardiff
eras.text: A producer's gig in Iceland ends with Le Bon locked down in Wales. The album she writes there gets her into Pitchfork's best of 2022.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon · Irish Times
years.h: Producing John Grant's Boy from Michigan
years.p: She is in Iceland working on [[John Grant|27ca9c68-650a-4659-b8ef-013e5698ff55]]'s record when lockdown closes the borders behind her, the Irish Times reported.

q: Cate Le Bon on Pompeii ruins (Irish Times)
years.src: Wikipedia: Pompeii · Album of the Year · BrooklynVegan: Pitchfork's · Irish Times
years.h: Pompeii: No. 20 on Pitchfork's best albums of 2022
years.p: Released 4 February 2022 on Mexican Summer. Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and ranked it No. 20 of 2022.
years.xp:
Jenn Pelly called it a 'wondrous sixth album' in the Pitchfork review. Metacritic scores it 85. It also placed 10th at Treble, 15th at Paste and 21st at Mojo.

It was written in Cardiff in the Victorian terrace she lived in 15 years earlier, with Tim Presley and producer Samur Khouja. Recording took in studios in Wales, Sydney and London; Stella Mozgawa plays drums, Euan Hinshelwood and Stephen Black play saxophone.

years.src: Exclaim!
years.h: 'Moderation' is the second single
years.p: Exclaim! reported 'Moderation' as the second single from Pompeii.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Producing Kurt Vile's 'Jesus on a Wire'
years.p: Wikipedia lists the song on [[Kurt Vile|e07a111e-4e8a-4651-a849-01ac60551ab2]]'s Watch My Moves among her production credits. Vile had sung on her Reward.

eras.title: Everybody's producer
eras.text: Having gone from one producer's desk to the next, she becomes the first outside producer Wilco has used since 2007, produces Devendra Banhart and Horsegirl, and releases the album she made after her breakup with Tim Presley.

years.src: BrooklynVegan: Wilco · Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Wilco let her produce Cousin, their first outside producer since 2007
years.p: Out 29 September 2023 on dBpm. Le Bon brought synths, drum machines and saxophonist Euan Hinshelwood into the band.
years.xp:
BrooklynVegan reported it was Wilco's first album with an outside producer since Sky Blue Sky. [[Jeff Tweedy|63287966-6021-474a-ba76-edc37a5f1b7c]] is quoted by Bandcamp Daily: 'I would love to work with Cate on anything.'

Tweedy has praised her guitar playing: 'Whenever I try to figure out her parts, they're way harder than they sound.' (Wikipedia)

years.src: Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Devendra Banhart, A. Savage and Kurt Vile again
years.p: She produces [[Devendra Banhart|0110e63e-0a9b-4818-af8e-41e180c20b9a]]'s Flying Wig, [[A. Savage|5bee43cb-a3a0-47bb-9cc6-662a90ce4380]]'s Several Songs About Fire and Vile's Back to Moon Beach.
years.xp: Banhart told Bandcamp Daily she is the only person he wanted to make the record with.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Bass and production on St. Vincent's All Born Screaming
years.p: She plays bass on two songs and gets additional production credit on four, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Michelangelo Dying · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Michelangelo Dying: the record after the breakup
years.p: Released 26 September 2025, with John Cale singing on 'Ride'. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp:
Wikipedia quotes Le Bon describing it as realising you have abandoned yourself in all-encompassing love, and the breakup as an amputation you don't want but know will save you.

It was planned for 2024 and delayed by illness and exhaustion after the relationship ended. Sessions took in Cardiff, Hydra, London and Los Angeles, with Samur Khouja producing.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily · Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Producing Horsegirl's Phonetics On and On
years.p: Drummer Gigi Reece said Le Bon is the first person the Chicago band let in as a fourth collaborator.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cate Le Bon
years.h: Dry Cleaning's Secret Love, and a St. Vincent single
years.p: She produces [[Dry Cleaning|8a74e5ea-6f68-49e1-951c-80d2291f7c3f]]'s third album; leftover sessions yield 'Always the Same' with [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]].
